''' Lateef Akinola Salako'''{{Audio|Lateef_Akinola_Salako.wav|listen}} [[Nigerian National Order of Merit Award|NNOM]], [[Order of the Niger|CON]] (5 July 1935 – 8 December 2017) was a Nigerian academic who was [[professor emeritus]] of [[Pharmacology & Therapeutics|pharmacology and therapeutics]] at the [[University of Ibadan]].

==Early life==
Lateef Akinola Salako was born on 5 July 1935 in [[Lagos State]], south-western [[Nigeria]].
He attended [[Methodist Boys' High School, Lagos]], where he obtained the [[West African Senior School Certificate Examination|West African Senior School Certificate]] in 1953.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.thenationonlineng.net/archive2/tblnews_Detail.php?id=45138|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=When Sultan donned the gown |accessdate=13 July 2015|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref>
He trained at the [[University College Hospital, Ibadan]] before he proceeded to [[University of Sheffield]] where he received a doctorate degree in 1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://muswen.org/Akinola%20Salako.html|title=Professor Lateef Akinola Salako|work=Musmen.com|accessdate=13 July 2015|archive-date=13 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713083632/http://muswen.org/Akinola%20Salako.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
He began his career in 1962, at the University College Hospital, Ibadan where he rose to the position of Senior Registrar in 1965, and in 1966,  he became a Medical Research Training Fellow, University of Ibadan. He was a Fellow in Clinical Pharmacology at the Department of Pharmacology and Therapeutics, [[University of Sheffield]] for two years, between 1967 and 1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.notablenigerians.com/?p=2244|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713161343/http://www.notablenigerians.com/?p=2244|url-status=usurped|archive-date=July 13, 2015|title=SALAKO, Lateef Akinola, Professor|work=Notable Nigerian|accessdate=13 July 2015}}</ref>
In 1969, he was appointed as Lecturer in Clinical Pharmacology, University of Ibadan, Ibadan where he rose to the position of senior lecturer in 1970, and in 1973, he was appointed a Professor of Clinical Pharmacology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/international/countries/africa/west-africa/nigeria/alumni|title=Alumni Association - University of Sheffiel|work=sheffield.ac.uk|accessdate=13 July 2015|archive-date=13 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713084324/https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/international/countries/africa/west-africa/nigeria/alumni|url-status=dead}}</ref>
In 1997, he was elected President of the [[Nigerian Academy of Science]] to succeed Professor [[Awele Maduemezia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |title=Members of Council |work=Nigerian Academy of Science |accessdate=7 June 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707061854/http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |archivedate=7 July 2015 |df= }}</ref>

Salako died on December 8, 2017, at the age of 82.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honor==
*Ogun State Distinguished Citizen Award, (1990){{Citation needed|date=May 2020}}
*[[Nigerian National Order of Merit Award]] (1992)
*[[Order of the Niger|Commander of the Order of Niger]] (2004)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nigeriavillagesquare.com/forum/archive/index.php/t-6162.html|title=[General] Back 2 School for OBJ|work=Nigerian Village Square|accessdate=13 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713124608/http://nigeriavillagesquare.com/forum/archive/index.php/t-6162.html|archive-date=13 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>
